chunk_findings.detail: The new pattern `python[0-9.]*[a-z]?(-dbg)?` only ever accepts **one** trailing ABI-suffix letter, but CPython's ABI flags compose: a build configured with both free-threading (`--disable-gil`, suffix `t`) and `--with-pydebug` (suffix `d`) installs its interpreter as `python3.13td` (or `python3.13dt`, depending on flag ordering). `_PYTHON.fullmatch("python3.13td")` returns `None`: `[0-9.]*` consumes `3.13`, `[a-z]?` consumes one letter, and the second suffix letter is left over (the `(-dbg)?` group cannot absorb it). Since `_describe_pid` only takes the "names its script" branch for a recognized interpreter, such a process falls into the fallback that shows the raw argv, so for a cmdline like `/long/scratch/.../venv/bin/python3.13td\0-m\0ddflow.infra.log\0...` the 200-char head (`_CMD_SHOWN`) is still entirely the long interpreter path and the identifying `ddflow.infra.log` part is still cut off — i.e. bug B3a4bf051b4 reproduces verbatim on exactly the "build-suffixed interpreter" class this hunk claims to fix. The added regression test cannot catch this because it only parametrizes the single-suffix names `python3.13t`, `python3.13d`, `python3-dbg`, `python`, and uses a short `/usr/bin/...` path.

chunk_findings.detail:
`claims_fix` is built as

```python
rf"\bfix(?:es|ed|ing)?\s+(?:bugs?\s+)?(?:[\w-]+\s*,\s*)*(?:and\s+)?"
rf"{re.escape(bug.id)}(?![\w-])"
```

Inside the repeated list group `(?:[\w-]+\s*,\s*)*` the comma is **mandatory** for every consumed element, and the id is only tried after that group and after an optional `(?:and\s+)?`. So the element joined by "and" is never reachable whenever anything precedes it: the group can consume `B29, ` but cannot consume `B31 ` (no trailing comma), so the cursor is left on `B31`, `(?:and\s+)?` fails to match `and`, and `B30` is compared against `B31`. Backtracking the group to zero iterations leaves the cursor on `B29`, which also fails.

Concrete input: bug id `B30`, item title `fixes bugs B29, B31 and B30`. `named.search` matches (so the item is not skipped), but `claims_fix.search` returns `None`, so `_show_bug` classifies the item under `mentioned_by` instead of `fixing`. That is exactly the convention the inline comment promises to support ("the verb, then the id or a list holding it": `"fixes bugs A, B and X"`), and the docstring names the same form. Consequently `ddflow show B30` (and any consumer of the `fixing` list, e.g. the fix-task view) treats the true fix task as a mere mention. Only the first element of an and-joined list, or an element sitting immediately after a comma (`fixes bugs B29, B30`), is matched; `fixes bugs B29 and B30` fails for `B30` as well.

(The rest of the file is internally consistent: the exit-code contracts in `loops`/`recover`, the truncation direction and `_render`-after-`_bound` ordering in `status`, the `not removed` filtering in `_dependency_findings`, the fallback→note mapping in `_launcher_findings`, the `shards - {log.shard.name}` self-exclusion in `_unknown_author_notes`, and the `inspect.signature` arity check in `render` all match their comments and docstrings.)

chunk_findings.detail: The truncation knob moved out of the module that used to be `ddflow.api.reporting`. `_bound` reads `STATUS_LIST_LIMIT` as a global of the new area module `ddflow.api.reporting.overview`, and `status` calls the `_load` name bound in that same module's namespace. The package `__init__` re-exports these names, so `ddflow.api.reporting.STATUS_LIST_LIMIT` still resolves and `import ddflow.api.reporting` still "works" — but rebinding the package attribute is now a silent no-op with respect to behavior. Concretely: a test that exercises the bounded MCP body (the 721k-char case this constant exists for) via `monkeypatch.setattr("ddflow.api.reporting.STATUS_LIST_LIMIT", 2)` and then calls `status(repo)` will still get lists sliced at 25, because `_bound` looks up `STATUS_LIST_LIMIT` in `overview`'s globals, not the package re-export; the same applies to any caller patching `ddflow.api.reporting._load` to stub the repo load, since `status` invokes the `_load` bound in `overview`, not the re-exported one. The stated mechanical verification (AST identity + byte-identical goldens) cannot catch this, because it is only observable through an attribute rebind on the old path.

chunk_findings.detail:
`worktree_entries` builds its untracked list with `_git_z(root, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z")`, i.e. with **no** `FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDE` / `_ours` filtering, and then applies the cost guard `if len(untracked) > MAX_UNTRACKED_HASHED: return None` *before* the `_ours(path)` filter inside the loop. The sibling helper in the same module, `_untracked_paths` (used by `_untracked_digest` and `diff_stat`), does the opposite: it passes `*FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDE` and therefore excludes `.ddflow/`. So the two halves of the same evidence disagree about what counts as "untracked".

Concretely: the whole reason `FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDE` exists (per its own comment) is that `.ddflow/` is *not* gitignored and was "creeping into a fingerprint"; `--exclude-standard` therefore does not drop it. Take a repository where `.ddflow/` has accumulated more than 512 untracked bookkeeping files (e.g. one event file per gate run) and no other untracked files. `_untracked_paths` returns `[]`, so `tree_fingerprint`/`_untracked_digest` behave normally; but `worktree_entries` sees `len(untracked) == 513 > 512` and returns `None`, so `source_tree(cwd)` silently returns `""` for every call even though none of those 513 files would ever be hashed (they are all dropped by `_ours`). Content-based evidence (`source_tree`/`commit_source_tree` comparisons, etc.) is thus disabled by ddflow's own state directory — exactly the class of "un-ignored directory full of artifacts" that `MAX_UNTRACKED_HASHED`'s comment says it wants to survive. Moving the guard after the `_ours` filter (or filtering the untracked list the same way `_untracked_paths` does) fixes it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/evidence.py:worktree_entries

chunk_findings.detail: `verify` and `verify_regression_test` read the gate runner through their own module globals: `from .runner import run_command_gate` (and `load_gates` on line 12) binds the name at import time. Before the split both names lived in `ddflow.services.gates`, so a caller/test that stubbed them via the package attribute (e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr("ddflow.services.gates.run_command_gate", fake)` or `monkeypatch.setattr(gates, "run_command_gate", fake)`) changed what `verify` called. After the move the package only re-exports the name; rebinding `ddflow.services.gates.run_command_gate` does not touch `mutation.run_command_gate`, so `verify` silently calls the real gate binary instead of the stub. Concretely, the probe referenced in the docstring (`tests/test_gate_verify.py`), which must control pass/fail per mutation to demonstrate the vacuous-pass guard, either now executes real commands (a test that intends to simulate `outcome == "failed"` instead gets the real outcome and can no longer assert `verified`) or fails outright; the same applies to any caller that stubs `load_gates` for `verify_regression_test`. This is a behaviour change the "AST-identical / byte-identical goldens" checks cannot see, and it is the exact package-attribute rebinding gap the move introduces.

chunk_findings.detail: These two tests impose contradictory requirements on a package attribute whose name equals an area module's name, so the suite cannot pass for `ddflow.api.reporting` and `ddflow.api.knowledge`. `test_an_area_is_reachable_as_its_module` requires `getattr(pkg, "status") is <the status submodule>` (likewise for `doctor`, `render`, `progress`, and knowledge's `recall`). But `status`/`doctor`/`render`/`progress`/`recall` are in `DEFINED`, and since the `__init__` may define nothing, each must be bound as a top-level def/class/assign inside some area module; `_top_level_names` collects exactly those, so `test_every_name_an_area_binds_is_the_same_object_on_the_package` requires `getattr(pkg, "status") is <that bound object>`. A function/constant is never the module object, so one of the two assertions must fail (whichever wins the last binding in the `__init__`): binding the area module as `reporting.status` makes `test_every_name_an_area_binds...` fail for the area that defines `status`; binding the defined object makes `test_an_area_is_reachable_as_its_module` fail. This directly contradicts the docstring claim "No area shares its name with a function: `gates.evidence` is the module" — that holds only for gates, not for reporting's `status`/`doctor`/`render`/`progress` nor knowledge's `recall`.

chunk_findings.detail: The package re-exports names *by value*, so rebinding a re-exported name on the package no longer reaches the code that reads it, contradicting the change's stated "same imports, no behaviour change" guarantee. Before the split, `ddflow.api.knowledge` *was* the defining module: functions such as `bug_found`/`bug_file_tasks`/`research_add`/`memory_add` read module globals like `BUG_REPORT_COMMAND`, `_load`, `Config`, `LINK_RELATIONS`, `recall`, etc. directly off that module, so a caller or test doing `from ddflow.api import knowledge as K; K.BUG_REPORT_COMMAND = "custom"` (or `monkeypatch.setattr(knowledge, "Config", fake)`, `knowledge._load = fake`) changed what those functions actually used. After this move, `bug_found` is defined in `ddflow/api/knowledge/bugs.py` and reads `bugs.BUG_REPORT_COMMAND`; `research_add` reads `research.Config`/its own `_load`, etc. Rebinding `ddflow.api.knowledge.BUG_REPORT_COMMAND` (the only public location that existed pre-split, and the only one a pre-existing test could have used) is now silently ignored, so such a test or caller exercises the real constant/helper instead of the patched one — a genuine runtime behaviour change, not a pure move. The in-file docstring documents the new patch-the-defining-module rule, but that confirms the semantic change and does not restore the old patch point.

chunk_findings.detail: Before the split, `_store` was a top-level function of the single module `ddflow/api/knowledge.py`, so *every* caller in that module (including `memory_list`) resolved it through the module's own globals. Tests/plugins that injected a fake index did so by rebinding the module attribute, e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr(ddflow.api.knowledge, "_store", fake)`, and every list/search function in the file picked it up. After the move, `_store` lives in the sibling area `lessons.py`, and `memory.py` binds it into its own globals at import time (`from .lessons import _store`). `memory_list` now reads that binding, not the re-exported package attribute. Concretely: with such a patch in place, `memory_list(repo, query="x")` still executes the real `_store(repo, log, cfg)` (the `store = _store(...)` call in the `if query:` branch) instead of the injected double, so the patch silently no-ops — the query path returns whatever the real search store produces rather than the stubbed data the test asserts on. This is the one name in this file whose patch semantics actually change: `O`, `IDS`, `csv_list` and `_load` were already imported from other modules before the split, so rebinding `ddflow.api.knowledge.<name>` never reached these bodies; `_store` did, because it was defined in the hot module.

chunk_findings.detail: `depth += {"[": 1, "]": -1}.get(ch, 0)` lets `depth` go negative when a parametrize value itself contains `]` — a case the sibling `_looks_like_several` explicitly declares supported (`t[x] y]` in its docstring, and it guards with `max(0, ...)`). Once `depth < 0`, every later `,`/`;` fails the `depth == 0` test and is never treated as a separator, so a comma-separated list is silently collapsed into one entry instead of being split. Concrete input: `--regression-test "tests/test_a.py::test_param[x]y],tests/missing.py::test_nope"`. `_split_outside_brackets` returns the whole string as one entry; `_unresolved_tests` then computes `path="tests/test_a.py"`, `names="test_param[x]y],tests/missing.py::test_nope"`, `wanted=["test_param"]`. `_looks_like_several` sees no whitespace outside brackets, so `tokens[1:]` is empty and it returns `False`; `_defines` finds `test_param` in `tests/test_a.py`, so the `not any(...)` arm is also `False`. The entry is therefore not added to `missing`, and `tests/missing.py::test_nope` is never resolved. `_unresolved_tests` returns `missing=[]` even though the second regression test does not exist, letting the bug be closed on a non-existent test. This is the same failure mode the `;` fix (B227585c781) was meant to eliminate — a list resolved as one node id. Clamping `depth` with `max(0, depth + {"[": 1, "]": -1}.get(ch, 0))`, as `_looks_like_several` already does, restores the split.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/regression.py:_split_outside_brackets

chunk_findings.detail: The guard for CONFIRMED/REFUTED is `not (finding.probe or finding.probe_output)`, so a finding whose `probe` is empty but whose `probe_output` is non-empty is accepted. The function's own docstring says "a CONFIRMED with no probe is an opinion wearing a label", and the emitted error text says the verdict "requires a --probe (and ideally --probe-output)", i.e. `--probe` is mandatory and `--probe-output` is supplementary. Concrete input: `Finding(question="q", verdict="CONFIRMED", probe="", probe_output="ran pytest and saw X")` reaches line 57, passes the validation, and `research_add` returns `O.ok("research.recorded", ...)`; the intended rule would instead return the `O.failed` message demanding `--probe`. The OR lets the optional evidence field substitute for the required one.

chunk_findings.detail: This package re-exports the moved names (`KEEP_RUN_LOGS`, `MAX_UNTRACKED_HASHED`, `EventLog`, `Config`, `run_command_gate`, …), but the moved functions read those names from their *own area module's* globals, so rebinding the package attribute no longer reaches any caller. Before the split there was one module, so a test or caller doing `monkeypatch.setattr(ddflow.services.gates, "KEEP_RUN_LOGS", False)` (or patching `gates.EventLog`, `gates.MAX_UNTRACKED_HASHED`, `gates.Config`, etc.) changed what `run_command_gate` observed. After the move, `run_command_gate` is defined in `ddflow.services.gates.runner` and resolves `KEEP_RUN_LOGS`/`EventLog` from that module's namespace; setting the same name on the package leaves the runner's binding untouched, so the gate still keeps run logs and still uses the real `EventLog` while the test believes it replaced them. The same silent no-op applies to every re-exported helper/constant, which directly contradicts the "no behaviour change" claim in the intent (the package docstring itself concedes "A REBINDING is not shared"). Any existing test/plugin that patches `ddflow.services.gates.<name>` will keep passing its old assertion only by accident or fail because the patched value is ignored.

chunk_findings.detail: The call `W.git(cwd, "hash-object", *paths)` passes untracked paths with no `--` separator, unlike every other argv list in this same file (`_untracked_paths` and `diff_stat` pass `--`, and `_hash_into` passes `"--"` before the same kind of path list). Git's option parser permutes and accepts options after positional args, so an untracked file whose name begins with `-` is consumed as an option rather than a file. Concretely, in a repository containing an untracked file literally named `-w`, `paths` is `["-w", "real.txt"]`; git parses `-w` as "write the object" and hashes only `real.txt`, so (a) `hash-object` WRITES a loose object into `.git/objects`, violating this function's own stated invariant that the observer "writes nothing", and (b) `len(ids) != len(paths)` makes the function fall back to the weaker names-only digest for the whole tree, silently degrading `tree_fingerprint` (so `stale_evidence` goes quiet) in exactly the repositories that have such a file. A file named `--stdin` would additionally make git read stdin instead. Adding the `--` terminator before `*paths` fixes it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/evidence.py `_untracked_digest`

chunk_findings.detail: `family_of` imports `family_for` from `...config` inside the function body instead of at module level. If a caller or test patches the package’s re-exported name (`ddflow.services.gates.family_for`) to control the family mapping, the patch is silently ignored: `family_of` always reads `ddflow.config.family_for` directly. For example, after `monkeypatch.setattr(gates, "family_for", lambda model, families: "anthropic")`, calling `family_of("unknown-model", cfg)` still returns the real, unpatched lookup, so any test relying on dependency injection for family resolution tests the wrong thing.

chunk_findings.detail: The move puts this code one package level deeper (the original module was `ddflow/services/gates.py`, i.e. package `ddflow.services`; the new file is `ddflow/services/gates/runner.py`, package `ddflow.services.gates`). Per the stated rule — "relative imports gain one dot because the code moved one package level down" — every *pre-existing* relative import must gain a dot, and the diff does exactly that for `..infra` → `...infra` (and for the in-function `...infra` imports of `tomlcfg`/`worktree`). The `testcmd` import, however, still has the original single dot. `testcmd` is not one of the gates domains this split creates (the plan lists `defs/run/evidence/outcomes`; `testcmd` is a dependency `gates.py` imported from, not part of `gates.py`), so it still lives at `ddflow/services/testcmd.py`. With `.testcmd` the interpreter resolves `ddflow.services.gates.testcmd`, which does not exist, so `import ddflow.services.gates.runner` raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ddflow.services.gates.testcmd'` at import time. Since `run_command_gate` is reached through the gates package re-export, every caller — `gate run`, the CLI/MCP `--help` and `tools/list` goldens the change claims are byte-identical — fails to import. The correct line is `from ..testcmd import suggested_test_command` (unless `testcmd.py` was also physically moved from `ddflow/services/` into `ddflow/services/gates/`, which the stated area list does not mention).

chunk_findings.detail: The exemption keys for the three moved knowledge writers were rewritten to `api/knowledge/bugs.py:_file_fix_task`, `api/knowledge/pairs.py:link_record` and `api/knowledge/bugs.py:bug_file_tasks`, but the knowledge package created by this change does not contain `bugs.py` or `pairs.py`. The change's own area list is `knowledge -> lessons/decisions/research/recall/memory`, and the sibling edit in the same diff confirms the file-name convention by moving `memory_add` to `api/knowledge/memory.py`. These functions therefore land in one of the five real areas (`link_record`, which "merges a lesson INTO the one it duplicates", is a `lessons`-domain writer; the `_file_fix_task`/`bug_file_tasks` pair is the `research`-domain bug-fix-task writer), so the defining path the coverage scanner sees (e.g. `api/knowledge/lessons.py:link_record`) never equals the dict key. Because `_calls_check_add`/`_appenders()` key writers by `<defining file path>:<function>` (as the surrounding assertions at lines 293-296 show), the `WRITERS_EXEMPT` lookup misses and the coherence assertion reports those writers as unexempted, failing the test. The fix is to key them by the area modules that actually exist (`lessons.py`/`research.py`, etc.), not the invented `bugs.py`/`pairs.py` paths.

chunk_findings.detail:
The test file is internally unsatisfiable for two of the three packages because the area-module names collide with names the same file insists the package must keep.

- `DEFINED["ddflow.api.reporting"]` contains `status`, `doctor`, `render`, `progress`; `DEFINED["ddflow.api.knowledge"]` contains `recall`.
- The stated split creates area modules named exactly `status`/`doctor`/`render`/`progress` (reporting) and `recall` (knowledge) — the intent lists those module names, and `test_an_area_is_reachable_as_its_module`'s own docstring uses `gates.evidence` from the same intent.

`test_an_area_is_reachable_as_its_module` asserts `getattr(pkg, "status") is <module ddflow.api.reporting.status>`. But once the `__init__` re-exports the original `status` name from whichever area defines it (`from .status import *` / `from .status import status`), the `IMPORT_FROM` bytecode stores the function into the package `__dict__` after importlib set the submodule attribute, so `pkg.status` is the function, not the module, and this test fails. Choose the other resolution — a bare `from . import status` so `pkg.status` stays the module — and `test_every_name_an_area_binds_is_the_same_object_on_the_package` fails instead: the area binds the function `status`, and it asserts `getattr(pkg, "status") is getattr(<area>, "status")`, i.e. module `is` function. There is no assignment of `pkg.status` that satisfies both, because a single attribute cannot be both the submodule and the re-exported callable. The same holds for `doctor`/`render`/`progress` and for `recall`; `gates` is unaffected only because `defs`/`run`/`evidence`/`outcomes` appear nowhere in its `DEFINED` list. Either the test as written cannot pass on the delivered tree, or the refactor silently rebinds `from ddflow.api.reporting import status` (and `recall`) from the function to a module — the exact break the change claims not to make.
